reason: Sunlight can drive evaporation from the ocean, a plausible first step in the water cycle.
expectation: The sun and ocean will produce water vapor or another step toward rain.

effect: Evaporation confirms the first step toward moving ocean water through the sky.
reaction: The result was predictable and clear.
reason: Air is a plausible way to move or cool evaporated water, but I am not sure which partner the game uses, so checking is useful.
expectation: The inspection should reveal how evaporation can lead toward clouds or rain.

alternatives.reason: I considered trying air directly, but its role is uncertain.

effect: Evaporation combined automatically with Air to make Clouds, confirming the next stage of the water cycle.
reaction: The distinction between invisible vapor and visible droplets was useful.
reason: Clouds and gravity suggest precipitation falling toward the land.
expectation: Gravity will help produce rain from the clouds.

effect: Clouds and Gravity produced Rainfall, bringing the water cycle down to the land.
reaction: The connection between gravity gathering worlds and bringing rain was satisfying.
reason: Rainfall on Earth is a plausible way to start water flowing across land toward rivers.
expectation: Rainfall and Earth will produce runoff or another stage toward rivers.

effect: Rainfall combined automatically with Gravity to make Rivers, showing that downhill flow is the next step.
reaction: Gravity's repeated role in the water cycle is clear, though Earth was not the expected partner.
reason: Rivers meeting the ocean are a plausible setting for sediment to build a delta.
expectation: The rivers and ocean may form a delta or an intermediate leading to one.

effect: Rivers cannot combine directly with Ocean; Earth and Sun are the available partners.
reaction: The compatibility feedback makes the next choices clearer.
reason: Earth is the more plausible partner for sediment carried by rivers toward a delta.
expectation: Rivers and Earth will produce sediment or a delta-building intermediate.

alternatives.reason: Sun is also compatible, but may relate to keeping water travelling instead.

effect: Rivers and Earth produced Sediment, a plausible ingredient for building a delta.
reason: Sediment meeting the ocean is a plausible next step toward forming a delta.
expectation: Sediment and Ocean will form a delta or an intermediate toward one.

alternatives.reason: This known compatible pair may advance the water-cycle goal instead.

effect: Sediment and Ocean formed a Delta, completing the river goal.
reaction: The explanation of slowing water and deposition made the result clear.
reason: Rivers and Sun are known to be compatible and may advance the remaining water-cycle goal.
expectation: This will help show water continuing its journey through the cycle.

effect: Rivers and Sun produced the Water cycle, completing the remaining goal and tying solar energy and gravity to the water’s continuing journey.
reaction: The self-sustaining cycle was a satisfying conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the water cycle tied the individual combinations into an understandable system and fulfilled the promise of a world that keeps moving without intervention.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying Rivers with Ocean was a minor disappointment: their meeting seemed a reasonable way to approach a delta, but the feedback required an intermediate instead.

surprise.text: I was surprised that Rainfall needed Gravity rather than Earth to produce Rivers; the explanation made downhill flow clearer.

arbitrary.text: Rivers plus Sun producing the entire Water cycle felt somewhat compressed, although the final explanation clarified their roles.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what the world makes without further intervention; the water cycle made that unfolding hook feel tangible.
